title: Hall Algebra Modules, Fock Spaces, and Geometric Actions

items.title: A one-vertex framed quiver variety and its Hecke correspondence

references.title: Hiraku Nakajima, Introduction to quiver varieties—for ring and representation theorists, §§2.2, 3.2, 4.4

items.statement:
Let $Q$ be the quiver with one vertex and no arrows. Its diagram is

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \node[circle,draw,inner sep=2.5pt] at (0,0) {$\bullet$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

For framing space $W=\mathbb C$ and dimension $v\in\{0,1\}$, put
$V_v=\mathbb C^v$. A **framed datum** is a pair of complex-linear maps
$I:W\to V_v$ and $J:V_v\to W$, subject to the moment equation
$I\circ J=0\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_v)$. The two framing maps are
drawn separately from the arrows of $Q$:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=stealth]
  \node (w) at (0,0) {$W=\mathbb C$};
  \node (v) at (3,0) {$V_v$};
  \draw[->] (w) to[bend left=22] node[above] {$I$} (v);
  \draw[->] (v) to[bend left=22] node[below] {$J$} (w);
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The group $G_v=\operatorname{GL}(V_v)$ of invertible complex-linear maps acts
by $g\cdot(I,J)=(gI,Jg^{-1})$. Fix the positive real stability parameter
$\zeta_R>0$ and, for this one-vertex quiver, call a solution **stable** when
$J$ is injective. Give the stable solution set its usual complex topology and
define $\mathfrak M(v,1)$ to be its quotient topological space by $G_v$.

For $v=0$ the solution set is a point, with coordinate algebra
$A_0=\mathbb C$; for $v=1$, writing $I(w)=iw$ and $J(z)=jz$, it is the
affine algebraic set $ij=0$ with coordinate algebra
$A_1=\mathbb C[i,j]/(ij)$. These are $\mathbb C$-algebras in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]. The action on data induces an action
on each $A_v$; write $A_v^{G_v}$ for its invariant subring of fixed elements.
Define $\mathfrak M_0(v,1)=\operatorname{Spec}(A_v^{G_v})$ using
[[def-affine-scheme-spectrum]]. An orbit of stable data maps to the point
whose prime ideal consists of invariant functions vanishing on that orbit;
this is the quotient map $\pi_v:\mathfrak M(v,1)\to\mathfrak M_0(v,1)$.
Let $0$ denote the point induced by the zero datum and put
$\mathcal L(v,1)=\pi_v^{-1}(0)$.

Let $S$ be the unframed simple datum with one-dimensional vertex space and
zero framing maps. A framed subdatum with vertex space $V'=0$ uses the same
framing space $W$ and zero maps $I':W\to0$ and $J':0\to W$. Its inclusion
uses the identity on $W$ and the unique map $\xi:0\to V_1$, compatible with
the data by $I=\xi I'$ and $J'=J\xi$; hence it forces $I=0$, while the
restriction of $J$ to $0$ is automatically zero. The quotient has framing
space $0$ and vertex space $V_1$, so its induced framing maps vanish and it is
$S$. The **Hecke correspondence** $P_{0,1}$ is the locus of pairs in
$\mathfrak M(0,1)\times\mathfrak M(1,1)$ obtained this way. Its two projection
maps are the source and target maps of the correspondence.

The degree-zero homology of a point is $\mathbb C$ with its point class,
using [[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]] and
[[thm-singular-homology-satisfies-dimension-and-arbitrary-additivity]]. When
$P_{0,1}$ and both spaces are points and the projections are identities,
define its fundamental-class correspondence map to send the source point
class to the target point class; the reverse map uses the same rule. This is
the point push-pull convention used here.

items.title: The A1 Nakajima varieties and the Hecke correspondence are points

references.title: Hiraku Nakajima, Introduction to quiver varieties—for ring and representation theorists, §3.2 Example 10 and §4.4

items.statement:
For the data of [[def-a1-nakajima-framed-quiver-data]],
$\mathfrak M(0,1)$, $\mathfrak M(1,1)$, $\mathfrak M_0(0,1)$,
$\mathfrak M_0(1,1)$, $\mathcal L(0,1)$, $\mathcal L(1,1)$ and $P_{0,1}$
are single points. The two projections from $P_{0,1}$ are identity maps of
points.

items.title: The A1 Nakajima Hecke correspondence gives the fundamental sl2 action

references.title: Hiraku Nakajima, Introduction to quiver varieties—for ring and representation theorists, §§4.2, 4.4–4.5

items.statement:
Use [[def-a1-nakajima-framed-quiver-data]] and
[[lem-a1-nakajima-varieties-and-hecke-correspondence-are-points]]. Let
$e_v$ be the fundamental class of $\mathcal L(v,1)$ in
$H_0(\mathcal L(v,1);\mathbb C)$, for $v=0,1$. Define $F$ by the
$P_{0,1}$ correspondence only from the $v=0$ summand to the $v=1$ summand,
and extend it by zero on $v=1$. Define $E$ by the reverse correspondence,
with Nakajima's sign $(-1)^{(d(0,1)-d(1,1))/2}$, only from $v=1$ to $v=0$,
and extend it by zero on $v=0$, where $d(v,1)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak M(v,1)$.
The preceding lemma says both dimensions are zero, so this coefficient is
$1$. Let $H$ act on the $v$-summand by $1-2v$. Then
$$E e_0=0,\quad E e_1=e_0,\quad F e_0=e_1,\quad F e_1=0,\quad H e_0=e_0,\quad H e_1=-e_1.$$
These operators define the standard two-dimensional representation of
$\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, the trace-zero $2\times2$ matrices with
commutator bracket.

items.title: Modules over a Hall algebra are unital algebra representations

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §§2.3–2.4

items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $H$ be a unital associative
$R$-algebra. An **$R$-linear representation of $H$** on an $R$-module $M$ is
a unital $R$-algebra homomorphism
$\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_R(M)$, where $\operatorname{End}_R(M)$ is the
ring of $R$-linear maps $M\to M$, with composition as multiplication,
$\operatorname{id}_M$ as unit, and scalar map $r\mapsto r\operatorname{id}_M$.
It defines the unital left action
$h\cdot m:=\rho(h)(m)$; its module axioms are those of
[[def-left-and-right-modules]]. When $H$ is a Hall algebra, this structure is
called a **Hall-algebra module**.

This term does not mean an object of the input category. An input object $A$
contributes a basis symbol $[A]$ to a Hall algebra, but that symbol by itself
specifies no representation on an $R$-module. The untwisted Hall algebra
instance is supplied by
[[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]],
[[thm-untwisted-hall-algebra-is-associative-and-unital]].

The zero $R$-module is allowed; its identity endomorphism is its zero map.
This definition gives an algebra action only. An action on a tensor product
requires additional structure, such as a specified coproduct.

items.title: A unital Hall algebra is a left module over itself

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §2.3

items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, and let $H$ be any unital associative
$R$-algebra that is a Hall algebra. The map
$\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_R(H)$ given by $\rho(a)(h)=ah$ is a
representation, so the left regular action makes $H$ a Hall-algebra module.

items.title: The generic Jordan Hall regular module carries the normalized Heisenberg Fock action

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §§2.3–2.4
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I §4, equation (4.5) and Remark 8

items.statement:
Use the category of finite-dimensional nilpotent Jordan-quiver representations from [[def-jordan-quiver-nilpotent-representation-category]]. Let $t$ be an indeterminate, $K=\mathbb Q(t)$, and $H_{J,K}:=H_{\mathrm{gen}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z[t]}K$ be the generic Jordan-quiver Hall algebra extended to $K$. Extend the exact isomorphism
$\Phi_t$ of [[thm-generic-jordan-hall-algebra-is-symmetric-functions]] to
$K$; its regular module is identified with
$\Lambda_K:=K\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\Lambda=K[p_1,p_2,\ldots]$. For a partition
$\lambda$, let $m_r(\lambda)$ be the multiplicity of $r$, set
$p_\lambda=\prod_{r\ge1}p_r^{m_r(\lambda)}$ and
$z_\lambda=\prod_{r\ge1}r^{m_r(\lambda)}m_r(\lambda)!$, and put
$p_\varnothing=1$. Write $\lambda\setminus(n)$ for the partition obtained
by removing one part $n$ when $m_n(\lambda)>0$; define
$m_n(\lambda)p_{\lambda\setminus(n)}=0$ when $m_n(\lambda)=0$. Transport
the Jordan Green pairing of
[[thm-jordan-hall-pairing-and-hall-littlewood-basis]] to $\Lambda_K$. On
power sums it is
$$ (p_\lambda,p_\mu)_G=\delta_{\lambda\mu}z_\lambda\prod_i(t^{\lambda_i}-1)^{-1}, $$
where $\delta_{\lambda\mu}=1$ if $\lambda=\mu$ and $0$ otherwise, and the
product runs over the parts of $\lambda$ with multiplicity. For $n\ge1$, let
$X_n$ be multiplication by $p_n$ and define
$$ X_n^{\dagger,G}p_\lambda=\frac{n\,m_n(\lambda)}{t^n-1}p_{\lambda\setminus(n)},\qquad P_n:=\frac{t^n-1}{n}X_n^{\dagger,G}. $$
Then $X_n^{\dagger,G}$ is the adjoint of $X_n$ for $(\ ,\ )_G$,
$P_n=\partial/\partial p_n$, and for each finite $N\ge1$ the assignments
$X_i\mapsto (p_i\text{-multiplication})$, $P_i\mapsto\partial/\partial p_i$,
and $Z\mapsto\operatorname{id}$ give a representation of the finite
Heisenberg Lie algebra $\mathfrak h_N(K)$ from
[[def-heisenberg-lie-algebra]]. The constant $1$ is the vacuum: $P_n1=0$,
and the vectors $\prod_{i=1}^N X_i^{m_i}1$, with nonnegative integer
exponents, span the subalgebra $K[p_1,\ldots,p_N]$; as $N$ varies, they span
$\Lambda_K$.

items.title: Arbitrary-framing A1 varieties and their conormal Hecke correspondence
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $W=\mathbb C^w$, $w\ge0$, and the no-arrow
one-vertex quiver. For $0\le v\le w$, stable data are
$I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$, $\dim V=v$, with $IJ=0$ and $J$ injective;
$g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)$ acts by $(gI,Jg^{-1})$. This extends the
$w=1$ convention in [[def-a1-nakajima-framed-quiver-data]]. The algebraic
orbit space is
$$M_v=T^*X_v=\{(S,A):S\in X_v=\operatorname{Gr}(v,W),\ \operatorname{im}A\subseteq S\subseteq\ker A\},$$
under $S=\operatorname{im}J$, $A=JI$. Put $a_v=v(w-v)$, so
$\dim X_v=a_v$, $\dim M_v=2a_v$. The map
$\mu_v:M_v\to\operatorname{End}(W)$, $(S,A)\mapsto A$, is projective;
its zero fiber $L_v=X_v$ is the zero section.

For $0\le v<w$, put $Y_v=\operatorname{Fl}(v,v+1;W)$ and write
$q:Y_v\to X_v$, $r:Y_v\to X_{v+1}$. The framed subdatum Hecke locus is
$$Z_v=\{(S\subset T,A):\operatorname{im}A\subseteq S,\ T\subseteq\ker A\} =\operatorname{Tot}\mathcal K_v,\qquad \mathcal K_v=\operatorname{Hom}(W/\mathcal T,\mathcal S).$$
Its image in $M_v\times M_{v+1}$ uses the same $A$ in both factors.
It is the conormal bundle to $Y_v\subset X_v\times X_{v+1}$ after applying
fiberwise negation in the second cotangent factor. Both projections are
projective, $\dim Z_v=a_v+a_{v+1}$, and
$Z_v\cap\operatorname{pr}_1^{-1}(L_v)=Y_v
=Z_v\cap\operatorname{pr}_2^{-1}(L_{v+1})$ scheme-theoretically.
All these constructions are $\operatorname{GL}(W)$-equivariant.

items.title: Excess intersection computes the A1 Hecke coefficients
items.statement:
Use $X_v,M_v,L_v,Y_v,Z_v,q,r,\mathcal K_v$ and $a_v$ from
[[lem-a1-arbitrary-framing-cotangent-hecke-model]]. All Chow groups have
rational coefficients. Intersect the fundamental cycle $[Z_v]$ with the
source zero section $L_v\times M_{v+1}\hookrightarrow M_v\times M_{v+1}$
by its refined Gysin map, keeping support on $Y_v$, and push along $r$.
The result is
$$r_*\bigl(c_v(\Omega_{Y_v/X_{v+1}})\cap[Y_v]\bigr) =(-1)^v(v+1)[X_{v+1}]\in A_{a_{v+1}}(L_{v+1})_{\mathbb Q}.$$
For the reversed correspondence, intersection with the other zero section
and push along $q$ gives
$$q_*\bigl(c_{w-v-1}(\Omega_{Y_v/X_v})\cap[Y_v]\bigr) =(-1)^{w-v-1}(w-v)[X_v]\in A_{a_v}(L_v)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
These are supported intersection calculations; they do not replace supported
classes by their potentially noninjective pushforward into $A_*(M_v)$.
The excess and Euler sequences used below are equivariant for
$\operatorname{GL}(W)$, although the asserted coefficient formulas are in
ordinary Chow groups.

items.title: Supported Chow convolution and its action for the A1 family
items.statement:
For $0\le u,v\le w$ use the smooth $M_v$ and projective maps $\mu_v$ of
[[lem-a1-arbitrary-framing-cotangent-hecke-model]], and put
$R_{uv}=M_u\times_{\operatorname{End}(W)}M_v$. A cycle on $R_{uv}$ is
regarded as a cycle with this support in the smooth product. Define
$$D\star C=(p_{13})_*\Delta_{M_v}^!(C\times D), \qquad C\in A_c(R_{uv})_{\mathbb Q},\quad D\in A_d(R_{vt})_{\mathbb Q},$$
where the diagonal identifies the two middle factors. Its degree is
$c+d-2a_v$ and its support is in $R_{ut}$. For
$\alpha\in A_k(L_u)_{\mathbb Q}$ define
$$C\star\alpha=(p_v)_*\Delta_{M_u}^!(\alpha\times C) \in A_{k+c-2a_u}(L_v)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
All pushforwards here are proper on the indicated supports. Convolution is
associative, the diagonal fundamental classes are units, and
$D\star(C\star\alpha)=(D\star C)\star\alpha$.
A cycle of degree $a_u+a_v$ therefore acts between the top zero-fiber
Chow groups. For $\alpha=[L_u]$, its action is equivalently the refined
intersection of $C$ with $L_u\times M_v\hookrightarrow M_u\times M_v$,
followed by pushforward with support to $L_v$.
These operations commute with the $\operatorname{GL}(W)$-actions on
ordinary Chow groups.

items.title: Arbitrary-framing A1 Hecke cycles realize the highest-weight sl2 module
items.statement:
For $W=\mathbb C^w$, $w\ge0$, and the no-arrow one-vertex quiver with
moment equation $IJ=0$ and stability $J$ injective, let
$$\mathcal V_w=\bigoplus_{v=0}^w A_{a_v}(L_v)_{\mathbb Q},\qquad b_v=[L_v],\qquad a_v=v(w-v).$$
Use the algebraic quotient and conormal Hecke cycles $Z_v$ of
[[lem-a1-arbitrary-framing-cotangent-hecke-model]] and the supported
convolution action of [[lem-a1-supported-chow-convolution-and-action]].
Define $F$ on the $v$-summand by $[Z_v]$ for $v<w$ and zero at $v=w$.
Define $E$ from the $(v+1)$-summand by the reversed cycle with coefficient
$(-1)^{a_v-a_{v+1}}=(-1)^{w-1}$, and zero at $v=0$.
Let $H$ act by $w-2v$ on the $v$-summand. Then
$$F b_v=(-1)^v(v+1)b_{v+1},\qquad E b_{v+1}=(-1)^v(w-v)b_v,\qquad H b_v=(w-2v)b_v.$$
The nonexistent endpoint terms are zero. These geometrically defined
operators satisfy $[E,F]=H$, $[H,E]=2E$, $[H,F]=-2F$ and give the
irreducible integrable highest-weight-$w$ representation of
$\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb Q)$. Scalar extension gives the corresponding
complex representation. All geometric maps and the action on ordinary
Chow groups are $\operatorname{GL}(W)$-equivariant. This theorem concerns
ordinary top zero-fiber Chow groups; it does not assert an action on the
entire equivariant Chow groups with coefficient parameters retained.

title: Hall Algebra Modules, Fock Spaces, and Geometric Actions: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The A1 Nakajima correspondence in the fundamental sl2 representation

references.title: Hiraku Nakajima, Introduction to quiver varieties—for ring and representation theorists, §§4.2, 4.4–4.5

items.statement:
For the one-vertex, no-arrow quiver with framing dimension one, the two
nonempty Nakajima fibres are points at $v=0$ and $v=1$. On their fundamental
classes $e_0,e_1$, the Hecke correspondence gives
$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

items.title: Two distinct one-dimensional modules over the generic Jordan Hall algebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §2.3

items.statement:
Let $K=\mathbb Q(t)$ and let $H_{J,K}$ be the generic Jordan Hall algebra.
By [[thm-generic-jordan-hall-algebra-is-symmetric-functions]],
$H_{J,K}=K[u_1,u_2,\ldots]$ as an algebra, where $u_r$ is the generator
corresponding to the class $u_{(1^r)}$. The assignments
$$\epsilon_0(u_r)=0\quad(r\ge1),\qquad \epsilon_1(u_1)=1,\quad\epsilon_1(u_r)=0\quad(r\ge2)$$
give two different one-dimensional Hall modules on the same $K$-vector
space $K$, by $h\cdot z=\epsilon_i(h)z$.

items.title: Degree-one normalization for the Jordan Hall Green pairing and Fock action

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2, §2.4, equation (2.9)
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Chapter I §4, equations (4.5)–(4.7) and Remark 8

items.statement:
For $p_1^r$ ($r\ge0$), the ordinary symmetric-function Hall form has norm
$\langle p_1^r,p_1^r\rangle_H=r!$, while the transported Jordan Green
pairing has norm $(p_1^r,p_1^r)_G=r!(t-1)^{-r}$. If $X_1$ is multiplication
by $p_1$, its adjoints therefore satisfy
$$X_1^{\dagger,H}p_1^r=r p_1^{r-1},\qquad X_1^{\dagger,G}p_1^r=\frac{r}{t-1}p_1^{r-1}\quad(r\ge1),$$
and the normalized Fock operator $P_1=(t-1)X_1^{\dagger,G}$ has the usual
derivative action $P_1p_1^r=r p_1^{r-1}$; both adjoints kill $1$.
Here $X_1^\dagger$ denotes the adjoint characterized by
$\langle X_1f,g\rangle=\langle f,X_1^\dagger g\rangle$ for the indicated
bilinear form; the diagonal nonzero power-sum norms make these adjoints
well-defined degree by degree.
